concepts.name: Biomolecule classes and monomers
concepts.summary: Recall the four major classes (carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids) and their building blocks.

concepts.name: Amino acid structure
concepts.summary: Describe the common alpha-carbon, amino group, carboxyl group and variable side chain of amino acids.

concepts.name: Peptide bond and primary structure
concepts.summary: Explain how amino acids link by condensation into a polypeptide whose sequence is its primary structure.

concepts.name: Enzymes as biological catalysts
concepts.summary: Explain that enzymes speed up reactions by lowering activation energy at an active site without being consumed.

concepts.name: Monosaccharides and fatty acids
concepts.summary: Recognise glucose as a key sugar and fatty acids as long hydrocarbon chains with a carboxyl group.

concepts.name: Metabolism overview: catabolism and anabolism
concepts.summary: Distinguish pathways that break down fuels to release energy from those that build molecules using energy.

concepts.name: ATP as energy currency
concepts.summary: Explain that ATP hydrolysis releases usable energy that is coupled to cellular work.

misconceptions.text: Enzymes are used up in the reactions they catalyse.
ATP stores energy in a stable form that the cell keeps in large reserves.
Energy is stored in the phosphate bond itself and released simply by breaking it.

concepts.name: Amino acid side chain properties
concepts.summary: Classify side chains as nonpolar, polar, acidic or basic and predict their charge and behaviour at physiological pH.

concepts.name: Levels of protein structure
concepts.summary: Describe alpha helices, beta sheets, tertiary folding and quaternary assembly and the bonds stabilising each.

concepts.name: Michaelis-Menten parameters
concepts.summary: Interpret Vmax and Km on a saturation curve and read their values from rate data.

concepts.name: Redox coenzymes NAD and FAD
concepts.summary: Apply the oxidised and reduced forms of NAD+/NADH and FAD/FADH2 when following metabolic reactions.

concepts.name: Glycolysis stages and net yield
concepts.summary: Trace glucose to pyruvate through the investment and payoff phases and compute net ATP and NADH.

concepts.name: Citric acid cycle inputs and outputs
concepts.summary: Follow acetyl-CoA through the cycle and account for CO2, NADH, FADH2 and GTP/ATP produced per turn.

concepts.name: Electron transport and ATP synthase
concepts.summary: Explain how NADH and FADH2 donate electrons to drive a proton gradient that powers ATP synthase.

concepts.name: Glycosidic bonds in carbohydrates
concepts.summary: Describe how glycosidic linkages join monosaccharides into disaccharides and polysaccharides such as starch and glycogen.

misconceptions.text: Km is the maximum rate of an enzyme reaction.
The citric acid cycle produces most ATP directly by substrate-level phosphorylation.

concepts.name: Lineweaver-Burk analysis
concepts.summary: Linearise kinetic data to determine Km and Vmax and compare enzyme behaviour.

concepts.name: Reversible inhibition types
concepts.summary: Distinguish competitive, noncompetitive and uncompetitive inhibition by their effects on apparent Km and Vmax.

concepts.name: Allosteric regulation and cooperativity
concepts.summary: Analyse how effectors and subunit cooperativity produce sigmoidal curves and shift enzyme activity.

concepts.name: Free energy of metabolic reactions
concepts.summary: Use standard versus actual free energy change to decide reaction direction and how coupling drives unfavourable steps.

concepts.name: Beta-oxidation of fatty acids
concepts.summary: Follow the repeated cycle of oxidation, hydration, oxidation and thiolysis and calculate acetyl-CoA, NADH and FADH2 from a given chain.

concepts.name: Regulation of glycolysis
concepts.summary: Analyse control of hexokinase, phosphofructokinase-1 and pyruvate kinase by energy charge and metabolites.

concepts.name: Gluconeogenesis and bypass reactions
concepts.summary: Explain how gluconeogenesis circumvents the three irreversible glycolytic steps with distinct enzymes.

concepts.name: Chemiosmotic coupling and P/O ratios
concepts.summary: Relate proton gradient magnitude to ATP synthesis and estimate ATP yield from glucose oxidation.

misconceptions.text: A reaction with a negative standard free energy always proceeds in the cell.
Gluconeogenesis is simply glycolysis run in reverse with the same enzymes.

concepts.name: Mechanisms of enzymatic catalysis
concepts.summary: Analyse how acid-base, covalent, metal-ion and proximity effects and transition-state binding produce rate enhancement.

concepts.name: Multisubstrate and irreversible inhibition
concepts.summary: Distinguish sequential from ping-pong kinetics and interpret mechanism-based inactivation from kinetic patterns.

concepts.name: Protein folding energetics
concepts.summary: Evaluate how hydrophobic effect, entropy and chaperones shape folding and how misfolding leads to disease.

concepts.name: Integration of fuel metabolism
concepts.summary: Evaluate how insulin, glucagon and tissue-specific pathways coordinate fuel use across fed and fasting states.

concepts.name: Metabolic control analysis
concepts.summary: Judge which steps control pathway flux using ideas such as near-equilibrium versus irreversible reactions and flux control.

concepts.name: Shuttles and mitochondrial transport
concepts.summary: Analyse how reducing equivalents and fatty acyl groups cross the inner mitochondrial membrane and affect ATP yield.

concepts.name: Respiratory control and uncoupling
concepts.summary: Evaluate how ADP availability, inhibitors and uncouplers alter oxygen consumption and ATP synthesis.

concepts.name: Ketone bodies and amino acid catabolism
concepts.summary: Analyse how fatty acid and amino acid carbon and nitrogen are routed to ketones, glucose or urea during fasting.

misconceptions.text: Enzymes work by changing the equilibrium of a reaction.
The rate-limiting enzyme is always the slowest step and alone determines pathway flux.
Fatty acids can be converted to glucose in animals via acetyl-CoA.

concepts.name: Critique of kinetic models
concepts.summary: Evaluate when Michaelis-Menten assumptions fail, such as tight-binding inhibitors, enzyme concentration comparable to substrate, or product inhibition, and choose a suitable model.

concepts.name: Systems-level flux analysis
concepts.summary: Assess flux distributions with stoichiometric models and isotope labelling and judge their limitations.

concepts.name: Design of enzyme inhibitors
concepts.summary: Design inhibitors using mechanism, kinetics and transition-state analogy and justify selectivity and potency measures.

concepts.name: Enzyme and pathway engineering
concepts.summary: Devise strategies to modify enzymes or reconstruct pathways to alter specificity, yield or regulation.

concepts.name: Metabolic reprogramming in disease
concepts.summary: Evaluate how altered glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation and lipid metabolism drive cancer, diabetes and inborn errors.

concepts.name: Thermodynamic and evolutionary constraints
concepts.summary: Judge why pathways have their observed structure, balancing yield, rate, thermodynamic feasibility and regulation.

concepts.name: Experimental design in bioenergetics
concepts.summary: Create experiments with appropriate assays, controls and inhibitors to test hypotheses about enzyme mechanism or mitochondrial function.

misconceptions.text: Michaelis-Menten kinetics apply universally to all enzymes under any conditions.
Inhibiting the rate-limiting enzyme of a pathway will always produce a proportionate drop in flux.
Cancer cells use aerobic glycolysis because their mitochondria are nonfunctional.
